name: AlGhamdi Company for Sanitary Wares       شركة الغامدي وشركاه للأدوات الصحية
note: Gate 2: sole KSA agent for American Standard/Ideal Standard selling toilets, basins, mixers, taps and bathroom fixtures. Sanitary ware is named by name in the Gate 2 hard-exclusions (construction materials), so it fails on category regardless of the corrected hybrid clause or any showroom/SHOP branding.

name: Ansar Group of Companies
note: Gate 6/2: Qatar holding entity spanning three co-equal pillars (Retail/Ansar Gallery, Hospitality/Hotels, Real Estate); a mixed conglomerate parent is excluded and the retail subsidiary Ansar Gallery is evaluated on its own separate row, not via this holding company.

name: Araboil
note: Gate 2: Arab Oil Fuel Company (est. 2022) provides vehicle fuel services, and fuel stations are an explicit hard-fail category. Domain also returns 503/dead, so Gate 4 independently fails; not an edible-oil or grocery retailer.

name: مكتبه جرير
note: The account name is Jarir Bookstore, a flagship Saudi-HQ'd retailer in fully approved categories (books, stationery, electronics) that the ICP itself names as a Gate 1 pass. The 'business directory' exclusion is a wrong-domain artifact (arabplaces.com is a directory, not Jarir); the entity qualifies and the domain should be corrected to jarir.com and deduped against any existing Jarir row.

name: Areej AL Khaleej  |  اريج الخليج
note: Gate 4/7: domain returns persistent 403/503 with no live storefront; independent re-check found no confirmable relocated site for this exact domain (only unrelated same-named auto/construction and fashion-influencer results). Per Gate 7 unconfirmable-defaults-OUT.

name: Armah Sports Company
note: Gate 2: Riyadh B2B fitness-facility designer/builder/operator (180+ GCC facilities), no product catalog or cart. Its consumer-facing brands are gyms (Optimo, B_FIT), which are fitness services, not product retail.

name: Arriyadh Roaster محمصة الرياض
note: Corrected Gate 2: confirmed live Salla DTC store with an extensive multi-category consumer catalog (coffee, Saudi coffee, matcha, capsules, accessories, bundles) well past the 50-SKU floor, coffee being a high-frequency F&B consumable. The coexisting wholesale/roasting arm does NOT disqualify (Go Fresh/Lazurde pattern); the cross-verification that re-excluded it wrongly applied the discredited 'any wholesale = fail' logic.

name: شركة عثمان الزامل واخوانه
note: Gate 2: Dammam trading company whose own store is branded 'Al-Zamil Store for Building Materials and Safety,' supplying building materials, safety and industrial goods. Construction-materials/industrial supply is a hard-fail category even at retail-store level.

name: Ashley Homestore | KSA
note: Gate 6: the underlying operation qualifies (Saudi operator Hamad M. Al Rugaib & Sons, Al Khobar 1958; live Shopify furniture store store.ashley.sa, broad catalog over 50 SKUs). But Al Rugaib is confirmed as a distinct Saudi furniture operator running its own-brand stores and e-commerce (alrugaibfurniture.com), so this foreign-brand storefront should likely consolidate under Al Rugaib rather than stand alone as 'Ashley KSA' -- genuinely unresolved without the IN-set.

name: Asklan Trading & Agriculture W.L.L
note: Gate 2/4: fundamentally a Doha B2B landscaping/irrigation contractor prequalified with QatarEnergy and government ministries; the 'Shop Now' cart is minimal/underdeveloped and its trading arm supplies landscape/irrigation materials and machinery, not a substantial dedicated consumer retail operation.

name: Aster Pharmacy - صيدلية استر
note: Gate 1: the KSA pharmacies run on a JV where UAE-HQ'd Aster DM Healthcare (Dubai, 1987) supplies the brand, 38-year healthcare systems and the shared myAster platform, with Al Hokair as local partner. This matches the explicit fail pattern ('run by a UAE-HQ'd group even with a local partner'), distinct from a Saudi conglomerate independently holding franchise rights.

name: ATHR Gallery
note: Gate 2: Jeddah contemporary art gallery doing artist representation, exhibitions, art fairs (Art Basel) and art-storage services. Fine-art gallery representation is not an approved retail category; the generic cart widget does not change the underlying business.

name: ايسوزو العيسى | Alissa Isuzu
note: Gate 2: Alissa Universal Motors, authorized Isuzu dealer in Saudi Arabia since 1985 selling pickups and trucks. Automotive dealer is an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Auto Mall
note: Gate 2: spare auto-parts dealer/distributor (since 1964) with showrooms in Dammam/Riyadh and 12 warehouses. Automotive parts is an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Autozone Balubaid
note: Gate 2: new-car dealership under Balubaid Group with 30+ branches across 13 Saudi cities selling Toyota, Hyundai, Honda, Kia, Isuzu plus vehicle financing. Automotive dealer is an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Auto Z Automotive Group W.L.L.
note: Gate 2: used-car dealership/showroom in Doha, Qatar. Automotive dealers are an explicit hard fail regardless of how live the operation is.

name: Baazeem Trading Company
note: Gate 2: live site is a pure B2B FMCG distributor brand-portfolio (brands, partners, distribution-channels nav) with no cart, checkout or consumer storefront anywhere and no own retail arm found. Wholesale/distribution as the sole consumer-facing identity is a hard fail even under the corrected hybrid clause.

name: Al Babtain Group
note: Gate 2/6: Kuwait conglomerate whose core is automotive dealerships (Nissan, INFINITI, Renault, plus OMODA/ZEEKR) alongside real estate, industrial (paints, lubricants/tires) and IT. No consumer retail division; automotive-led mixed conglomerate parent is excluded.

name: باك كمفورت - Backcomfort
note: Gate 3: confirmed live Saudi store (Mada/Tamara/Tabby/STC Pay checkout) but the catalog is a narrow low-repeat durable niche -- massage chairs, office chairs, recliners and sleep products. Maps to the confirmed mattresses-only/lighting-only narrow-repeat-purchase fail; big-ticket items that cannot sustain ongoing CDP engagement.

name: Al Baladi Holding
note: Gate 6/4: mixed Qatar holding (hypermarkets/supermarkets alongside hotels and limousine transport) whose own domain is a corporate portfolio site with no cart/checkout. The transactional retail brand Baladi Express is separately captured IN, so this holding row correctly fails.

name: Balsam Medical Care
note: Gate 2: Saudi hospital/medical-complex group (general medicine, pediatrics, OB/GYN, dentistry, dermatology, orthopedics) where pharmacy is one part of a hospital-led portfolio, not a standalone retail pharmacy chain. Healthcare/clinics is a hard fail; the domain is also a login-gated portal, not a storefront.

name: Balsharaf Group
note: Gate 4: genuine FMCG group with a real physical food-store retail arm (since 1955), but no live transactional online store or 50k+ consumer app was findable and the corporate site has no cart. The retail arm is real (so not a Gate 2 fail) but fails the digital-channel gate.

name: Bastana International Company Ltd
note: Gate 2/4: primarily a Saudi B2B landscaping/garden design-build-maintain contractor for government/private projects (6M+ sqm maintained). Its online plant nursery is a thin, non-transactional add-on (no visible cart/pricing/checkout), not a substantial dedicated retail operation, so it fails the corrected hybrid test the same way Saudi Radwa did.

name: BATOOK HOLDING COMPANY
note: Gate 2: chewing-gum manufacturer (Nova, Klast, Miska) with manufacturing, investment, and traditional/modern trade distribution arms. The corporate site has no consumer cart/checkout/pricing; 'retail' here means trade channels selling to other retailers, not its own consumer chain -- manufacturing plus wholesale is a hard fail.
